Paragraph: Summary of Passage: People in this material world often seek immediate success in fruitive activities, leading them to worship powerful entities for quick, temporary gains.
Situation/Problem_Faced: The human tendency to prioritize instant gratification and short-term success over long-term spiritual growth.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Krishna observes: 'kanksantah karmanam siddhim yajanta iha devatah, ksipram hi manusye loke siddhir bhavati karmaja' (Those desiring success in fruitive activities worship demigods; human success from work comes quickly in this world).
Outcome/Resolution: Distinguishes between short-term material rewards and enduring spiritual fulfillment.

Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Instant Gratification vs. Long-Term Valu: Choosing quick fixes over sustainable, deep transformation
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Material Attachment: Over-investing emotional energy in temporary outcomes
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Patience in Personal Growth: Understanding that meaningful progress requires sustained effort

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Kanksantah karmanam siddhim (Desiring quick success from fruitive work)
Ksipram hi manusye loke siddhir bhavati (Quick results are obtained in the human world)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: Seeking quick material results leads people to worship secondary powers, but these gains are temporary compared to eternal self-realization.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: Chasing instant gratification provides fast but fleeting relief; true psychological maturity involves foregoing quick fixes in pursuit of lasting well-being.
